terms.gloss: an ideal: the pattern of a thing seen by the mind
evidence: Cic. Or. 18: īnsidēbat in ejus mente speciēs ēloquentiae (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Off. 3.81: speciēs, fōrma et nōtiō virī bonī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Cicero’s word for Plato’s ἰδέα (Ac. 1.30). The noun “ideal” is a modern sense; Latin names what the ideal is of: speciēs virī bonī, the ideal of a good man. The everyday senses of speciēs are sight, appearance, outward show and beauty, and in logic a kind (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: the ideal form of a thing
evidence: Cic. Or. 43: excellentis ēloquentiae speciem et fōrmam adumbrābimus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Beside speciēs, the perfect shape of a thing; ordinarily shape, figure, appearance and beauty.

terms.gloss: a model, a pattern to copy
terms.comment: Traupman’s word for an ideal: the model one copies (see model).

phrases.latin: hanc illī ἰδέαν appellābant, nōs rēctē speciem possumus dīcere
phrases.english: they called it idea; we can rightly call it species

phrases.latin: īnsidēbat in ejus mente speciēs ēloquentiae
phrases.english: an ideal of eloquence was fixed in his mind

sources: Lewis & Short: species · Lewis & Short: forma · Lewis & Short: exemplar · Lewis & Short: idea

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
